author: Aaron
text:
My second chart for the day concerning the IT’s activities:

Below is the 4hr chart showing the supply I am working with:

Below here is the 30 min chart:

1. The ITs buy heavily here, but why would the ITs be doing this? I can see a few reasons. Look to the right, we see a huge RN.9000, we all know there will be orders there, and if we know, they sure as hell will! The ITs buy into this zone collecting a truck load of buy stops from all the traders who were attempting to fade the price level.

2. Now, remembering the ITs have just bought price north, what follows momentum, normally LTF retailers, following the herd, I know this is not a lot of LQ in the big scheme of things, every bit adds up I guess. These BO buyers were more than likely trailing their stops, depending on where one entered, one could have been stopped for a small win or a loss, this will give the ITs some sell stops to buy into. Number 2 is a very important area because I believe this was a supply area created to be broken and fool traders to short there. The small move south was ITs placing some sells into the market.

3. Price has stopped out a load of BO buyers, and broken some LTF demands giving a lot of sell stops to the ITs, but something else here too, the RN 9000 has been faked again, this time south. The ITs stopped out the traders who were trying to fade the big number, instead they got stopped for the LQ which gave the ITs even more buying power using the stopped traders’ sell stops.

4. Remember back to number 2, this level was created there to be faked, there would be very little IT’s limit orders placed here if any, the only people selling here are the traders unaware of the games! This level was faked, thus giving the ITs buy stops, to sell into, and with the HTF supply so very close, they will throw a nice sized order into the market pulling price south.

5. With this big drop in price the ITs know all kinds of traders would be joining this drop, for example: Traders who see the HTF level originally would now be nicely short, traders who missed it by a few candles and jumped in late (chasing price), BO sellers etc… All of this momentum south was nicely stopping out all traders who traded the momentum north on number 4. We also see the RN broken again, this would have had a nice bit of LQ for the ITs (sell stops). So we have reached the big figure and engulfed number 3, nice work by the ITs, time to take a little profit, if they want to take profit, they need some traders who will take their buy orders from them as they are nicely short now. Firstly we have the sell stops From the RN, the BO sellers who entered on the BO of the RN, this is enough to give them a little breathing space and bank a few 100 million.

6. The ITs are heavily short here and very pleased with themselves, they have now again faked the RN 9000 once again to collect the buy stops to sell into, these poor traders who were trying to buy and sell around this RN got whipsawed! The ITs know there will some BO buyers at the RN too, this will also give them some more to sell into to continue their path south, not forgetting the numerous LTF supplies the ITs have engulfed and collected LQ too.

So to answer my own question, I do believe the ITs trade against themselves, if we think about it logically, how would they be able to compress price without trading against their positions, or engulf and return etc...

author: HotRod
text:
We are told the reason the markets exist is to give value to an instrument. All the market participants with interest in an instrument come together to give the correct value to that instrument. This may have been true in the 1600s, but now this is a bunch of BS and assumes everyone obeys the law and follows exchange rules.

If everyone had the same access to the same information, then the market would truly be random because price could then only reflect all the differing opinions about that information. But what about information that would have an obvious effect on price? If everyone had the same opinion then the market would be "broken" because no one would want to take the other side of the trade. But where is the profit in that? If the true reason the markets exist is to find value, then they would make information freely available. They don't do that because the markets wouldn't work. The markets only exist so the people at the top of the money chain stay on top.

Information is the most valuable commodity in this world and is kept in the closest of circles until it can be used for profit. The people who have it are the ones at the top of the worlds industries, and the banks that hold and loan them their money. You also have to include top governmental positions (financial) since the people who hold them are usually "experts" that were CEOs and such. These people have relationships with each other and we would be extremely naive (American public) to believe they don't use that for their own gain.

One of biggest things I took away from the book Trading and Exchanges is the concept of informative prices. Prices become informative when informed traders trade. Now this doesn't really help us take a position because there is no way of knowing when these traders are trading. But the concept does allow us to form a better view of the markets participants.

There are 3 types of traders: informed traders, uninformed traders, and uninformed traders who believe they are informed.

Informed traders: These traders have information that will effect the real world supply and demand, and are able to take positions in the instrument's market before the information has its effect. In the forex market it would be things like interest rates and policies, or major changes in a country's leading industry. This can also be the banks holding the order book, friends and family who were given tips, or people who are able to use a chart to see where these informed traders are taking positions.

Uninformed traders: People who just trade as a hobby, gamblers, News traders, people who only watch the right edge of the chart and trade off emotions.

Uninformed who believe they are informed: Pretty much anyone who gets their "education" from a book. You know, indicator traders, system traders. would throw people who subscribe to these news agencies here as well since they usually end up getting fleeced. Some of these people probably make money, but most don't.

The idea here is that if the market was only made up of informed traders, then they would never be able to take a position. If all the informed traders know the same bullish information, then none of them are going to sell. This is where uninformed traders come in. So, how do they entice enough people to take the other side of their trades? First they put the perception out there that there is all kinds of money to be made in the stock market. (Economics class anyone? Ok that may be too far, but i doubt it. I'd say they have connections to the gov. positions that develop the curriculum) Then they herd us like a bunch of cattle. They know humans feel safer when in groups, and if they can get enough people following a certain way of thought, then others will follow.

So what do they use to herd us into groups so they can profit from us?

Scheduled news releases with the CNBCs of the world to make people feel informed is probably the biggest. I'm going to guess the second biggest way is with all the "education" out there. I believe the material constantly being put out there comes from these same informed traders, either through straight up funding for it or some other way. But even if not, its out there, and can be used to fill their orders. How long has S/R been out there? Since Wyckoff in the 30s? Earlier? What about trend? Trend lines? All the different patterns that are taught and where to enter on them? And lots more. The stronger the following each "herding tactic" has the more profitable it is for the informed traders. The market mechanics of S/R is there yes, but it isn't going to have that strong of effect on the market, when it works its because the informed ITs are behind it. Yes it all works sometimes, until it doesn't. It serves two purposes, first to fill their orders and then to save them money when moving price to their take profit positions. What do all the educators preach? You have to trade it EVERYTIME and use good money management. All of this is herding. And don't forget that evil little ticker on the hard right edge for all the emotions. That gets manipulated as well, and always right into informed traders orders.

Informed traders are always going to stick together. They are out to make as much money as they can. And they aren't going to make much money by battling each other. They want the easiest prey possible, and the prey will always be uninformed. Whether they use their "herding tactics", or whether they want to "eat" their own and feed them some bad information, either way they are uninformed. There is always a battle, but the informed will always know they are going to win.

Vogon, on your chart the sellers were informed, and the buyers weren't. Simple I know, but its best that way. Any thing else and your head will become clouded with unneeded thoughts which will lead to frustration. We can paint any picture really, because there is honestly no way of knowing. And being on the weekly chart it coulda been a central bank with bad information, or maybe some uninformed ITs. This was back in 07/08 when all the economic trouble began. Look where it peaked. It peaked in Nov of 07, so whoever it was had their info at that time and started selling. Any bullish info put out between that peak and the drop was all manipulation to fill their orders and trap the buyers.

If you have ever read reminiscences of a stock operator, then you know Jesse Livermore made a killing off of the drop that caused the great depression. He traded by being able to read the ticker tape and knowing when the market was being manipulated, then jumping in with the manipulators. We would be very naive to think that it no longer gets manipulated.

So how can we profit from all this? I'm still working on that

Knowing all

this is great, but on the hard right edge the informed traders and uninformed traders are ever evolving and changing. The market environment is never the same with there being times when there are tons of news coming out, and other times when there is a news drought. Especially in forex since there isn't as many news events. This is why its seen as being a more technical market, they need someone to fill their orders. There is also the issue of time frames. The informed traders on the HTFs may or may not be the same ones on the LTFs.

In times of news droughts and on the LTFs the only real informed traders I can think of are the market makers. The people who can see the limit order book and know where the big orders are is the LTF uninformed traders enemy. But even he has weaknesses because he can only see limit orders, he doesnt know what market orders are going to come in and endanger his position. There could be a large IT out there who hits the market with a big market order to test a price level to see how dense the orders are there.(i believe this is one explanation for the engulf.) There are multiple market makers in the forex market in each instrument. They compete to provide liquidity to the uninformed traders. They don't have to provide liquidity if they don't feel they will make money on it. (only the NYSE specialists have to provide when they don't want to, and they can just widen the spread to protect themselves.) So if the market makers believe they have an informed trader entering the market they will just sit on the sidelines. If they were wrong the worse that happens is a competitor makes money and they don't. If they believe there are uninformed traders entering the market they will happily provide liquidity because they know chances are they will be in profit very shortly. I don't know the tactics the market makers use to discern the difference, but that is our job as well. I would say they can tell by how the orders come in or maybe make deals to get info.

Just by thinking about the tactics that uninformed traders use, and knowing how the informed traders use those tactics against them should give us a way to piece together the story of price. If we know where uninformed traders are going to put their orders, and we know that informed traders need those orders to trade, then we know where the battle is going to take place. If price doesn't do what the uninformed trader expected and he lost then there is a good chance an informed trader was active there, and then we just use the tools that IF and the gang have taught us and that will tell us to take action or stay on the sidelines. If price does do what the uninformed trader expected, then the informed trader sees an opportunity for more profit.

When I get time I want make a chart showing how I see it, but its late and im tired. GL trading today everyone!!!

Hi Guys,

Sorry I was not active yesterday in the forums! I was working with the FOREX tester, what a marvelous tool that is! Thanks to all the posters here, what a fantastic learning experience this will be.

Hot rod, what a fantastic post my friend! Please do more, I am sure we all benefit!

Here is my next attempt at identifying the ITs mindset, one thing that always sticks is: ‘Orders move the markets’ without them, the market is still. So if orders move the markets, and we know these orders are mainly the ITs, they clearly need other orders to trade against, if not they would not make any profit.

Below is the 4hr chart showing the demand level I am working with, the demand is after the red line.

Below is the 30 min TF, this is what I will be working with:

1. Here we see the ITs accumulating buy orders here I believe, remember if the ITs do not have the orders to buy and sell to, they will not profit. Look at the candle with the tail south, this is the tricks the ITs play, fooling retailers to sell, and then they quickly reverse the price collecting all the BO sellers stops giving the ITs some LQ. Another thing to bear in mind and which I believe is looked at quite a lot, especially by retail traders is the RN.50 there will be a lot of traders attempting to fade this level, thus with the spike down, they were stopped out and the ITs collected their sell stops for extra buying power. This area really interests me, look at just before the candle with the tail, we had bullish/bearish candles, can you imagine how much panic was in the market during this whipsaw! Traders would’ve been long then short, short then long, what a headache, but the ITs knew they were doing this to collect even more LQ.

2. The ITs have bought hard and this is where they first entered the market long, and in the process stopping out tons of traders, these traders are the ones who were short, and thought the market would not stop going down, thus forcing them into a loss depending on where they sold, and collecting their buy stops, nice for selling into. Also with a move like this, can you imagine how many LTF supply zones were engulfed, giving the ITs more buy stops to sell into, then finally, momentum, all the traders who saw price rising from a nice demand area, jumped in late thinking it would not reverse, and when price does eventually reverse @ supply they panic and panic in the markets makes traders close their positions when really they should be watching what PA is telling them.

3. The reverse did come, and the ITs were more than likely taking a little profit here, as they had a enough LQ to sell into.

4. The ITs began buying lightly considering we are in the Asian session, to attract a lot of BO buyers and this would without a doubt make traders jump on the bandwagon long again, thinking this was just a pull back, the big move is coming soon. A thing we have to bear in mind here though, where would the ITs get their LQ to push price up? To the next demand which was below.

5. This I believe is the source of the original move up and there are some limit orders left there that were not executed from the ITs, so they push price down, and push it down hard! This attracts BO sellers, and scares the crap out of all those traders long, either forcing them to take a small win or getting caught in the ‘hope’ trap, then they would have more than likely been stopped out for a loss or BE, the ITs know this. This would be the ITs second entry into the market long, now they are quite heavy long.

Cheers all

text:
Ok here goes my second attempt for the day, I don’t know about anybody else but this task really gets my brain thinking logically, which is rare for me!!

This example is especially interesting, why? I will explain after the usual breakdown.

Below is a 4hr FTR zone, one which engulfed the high and has a high probability of a reaction, do not pay attention to the zones before the red line, it is the one after I am focusing on.

Below is the 30 min TF

1. The ITs spike the RN.3600, were they testing the level here for buying pressure? I believe they may have been. Can you imagine how many traders went long on that bullish pin bar at the RN, I would have done a few years ago. Keeping these traders who went long on the bullish pin bar in mind, let’s dig deeper into what other reasons these spikes formed. I have already said they may have been testing the area, another thing that they may have been doing was a shake out of the buyers who were trying to fade the RN and also the BO sellers, think about how much LQ this would have given the ITs. We have sell stops from the traders long at the pin, we have BO sellers buy stops from the traders setting BO orders short at that area, and finally we have traders’ who faded the level with their stop just beneath the RN asking to be stopped out. So this gives the ITs buy stops to sell into to begin the move south, plus when they hit the sell stops of all those buyers price would move south even more.

2. The ITs pushed price down to the next demand which happened to be in the 4hr FTR, so a high probability area for LQ, and the ITs see this. With price being sold by the ITs into demand, there were no doubt BO sellers following the herd down to demand just waiting to be stopped out by the ITs, this gave them some buy stops to work with to help price up. The ITs hit demand and began putting in the first order long here, with the help of the buy stops from the sellers and the original buyers at the demand, this was quite an easy buy for them.

3. Here the ITs want to clearly be the only big buyer in this market, so they want to confuse all who are trying to join, look at what the ITs did here, they whipsawed price up and down, stopping all the unaware traders out, and leaving them wondering where the hell price is going, this is clearly want they wanted. Another interesting thing here is the RN, now the ITs clearly have broken this level @2 and there will be a lot of traders trying to short the retest on the LTFs, the ITs know this and they also know there will be BO buyers in and around this area, so here the ITs used the traders’ buy stops who were trying to buy the BO for them to sell into, with this in mind we also have trader who are short the RN on the retest. This will give the ITs extra momentum with these sells helping push price down.

4. To add to the confusion the ITs pushed price down as already said, but why would they do this? It is confusing; we are at demand, why are they selling?? The reason is they want this confusion, they like it, it is the retail side who do not. This move down will scare traders who were long from the demand closing their trades near breakeven creating sell stops for the ITs to buy into, not only this, there were no doubt small LTF demand levels engulfed and a lot of sell stops collected, again for the ITs to buy into, here would be the second long into the market, by now I believe the ITs are quite heavily long, with these big buys going into the market price rallies.

5. The buys were in the market now, but clearly not enough as we see the IT’s consuming the oncoming supply, notice the 2 wicks above lapping up them sell orders to bring price down, whilst doing this, the ITs know that the previous rally would have attracted a lot of BO buyers with sell stops just waiting to be taken. Now with the ITs consuming this supply, they know that a lot of traders jumped on the momentum long, why wouldn’t they? We are at demand. So what do they do? They sell into this confusing poor retailers once again. Bearing all this in mind we were also at the RN, it would be anyone’s guess to how much LQ would be there again with new traders trying to trade the BO and fade the price level.

6. Much the same as 4

7. Much the same as 5

Something I wanted to add to this chart, notice what I said in my own journal about consumption of orders, and the possibility of entering the market on the return, we see this here. We consume supply orders @5 then drop back to source, a nice long entry here being aware of oncoming supply, could have made a nice scalp. But we had one clue here with an entry @ 6, look at the PA once we entered, it was CP, not a good sign.

We did eventually see an engulf of the highs and a nice return to a DP in green.

author: AERO
text:
Ifmyante wrote: We will, however, battle with the monsters, and we will win, without darkening our souls a shade

I definitely agree that for ITs using algo's, programmed by their intentions and rules definitely relieves them of time and imprecision. Though i would just like to point out, basing on my recent research, using algo's doesn't necessarily mean HFT (High Frequency Trading) as it is very commonly believed now a-days. A light speed trading they call it, and the ones that have planted their asses the closest to the trading terminal, have the fastest execution. Why would you fight for nano seconds?

As i see, most of these highly technically educated people are very brilliant at working out the best codes for taking the profit out of the market. Though from what i have read and understood, their mindsets ONLY understand the markets microstructure and mostly just opt to gain return with tactical tricks.

Common practice is them offering liquidity to other manual traders, entering with a market order. Once the HFT's pending order is filled, they close it in a split of a second, just to profit on the spread the retailer has paid to get into the trade. Ofcourse there are psychological tricks that go around these liquidity offering twists, but nothing is intended for a longer period of investing.

That is where the tight spreads come from! HFTs competing between each other and getting fees just for supplying liquidity to dealers.

Simply put, there is no long term strategy HFTs live by. A tactic is hardly successful if it isn't sufficiently applied within some bigger/higher-picture plan. Plan being the engulfing signals and other.

Now, if u get a trader that understands the basics of HFT codes and the strategy, you get a golden boy, who can program and hugely lessen all the needed work and especially the risk. ~~~

Imagine: We hava a buying range. creting compression and a consistent buying in small lots is requiered,before we give a signal to break out and advance to next level. Doing it manually, well...:P Its exhausting, to say the least. I know i would program the algo, tu buy small lots with market orders on the way up of the range, and just let the algo put pending longs, while price is retracing within a move. (If there is a scenario to break long.)

Big orders don't get a fill, and even more, you dont want to bust open the range, and bring confusion to other ITs faces, while they are happily loading their cargo. (I believe there are even upper lot limits for market orders, with some brokers.

~~~ This is very interisting article that sheds light on alot of what HFTs are considered to be! www.forbes.com/sites/richardfinger/2013/...aders-and-investors/

These topic has been hot since 2010 the FLASH crash. Contemplating wether these algos are of risk to the stability of market! From what i read, people kept unplugging their sweet HFTs algos as they in horror observed DOW plunging. That way they created volatility, price droped presumeablly to a targeted level and resumed back up! (I havent checked since i got no DOW with my broker.)

Those in-the-moment-profit guys, considered it risky since they had no clue what was going on, and with such speed of price droping, their light speed pending longs would not get the return either. They dont even want to think about the loss scenario, due to over laveraging....

From my understanding, price has simply pushed to target and retraced. Driven by the IT traders (or algos), that were fully aware of the target for retrace. Long term strategy won again.:D

If u have ever played chess - you probably know why.:)

just my 2 nano pips AERO

author: pucci
text:
Morning Everyone,

For a while now already I have been obsessed to get myself to think like an IT. Yesterday after I called it a day and especially due to IF’s comment on the charts; “think like an IT, think like an IT, think like an IT…” was playing over and over in my head even when I was asleep!

This morning, while I was preparing to start analyzing Area 5 (In my Journal), my mind asked a set of questions:

1- Is it possible that a five year old area would still hold left over orders?

2- If I were an IT, would I have left pending orders there for so long? Especially that the framework in the mix of fundamental, geopolitical, economical, financial… etc... climate was surely different?

3- If the answer to the above questions is yes, wouldn’t brokers, market makers, liquidity providers and what have you, make a killing by just charging for those pending orders? (Just imagine the accumulated returns on a certain five year old level)

4- Wouldn’t we know about such interest payment requirements?

Certainly after more such questions we come to the conclusion that it has to be a definite “NO” for the first two above.

Ok…. So hypothetically, why would a five year old level react the way it does? It must be NEW orders there then. But what’s there? Older levels… hmmmm

Now at this point and due to my previous career, I shifted my thought process back into the corporate world. Isn’t that what ITs are really? So they must think in terms of Daily, Weekly, Monthly, quarterly, semiannually & annually…. With cycles in between, some longer others shorter.

Now let’s step out of our trading shoes for a while and think in terms of consumerism. Imagine I was an avid car collector and Bugatti was giving away free Veyrons, with the only requirement to get one being to stand in line and waiting your turn. How long do you think the Q will be by the time I get there? Will there be enough cars left by the time I get there? Will the plant have enough cars to satisfy all the demand? At what point will the manufacturer start pricing the product again? On the other hand imagine if that same product was priced at 1 trillion, would there be any demand for it? Supply? Parts? After Sale Customer service?

So there is a tipping point isn’t there i.e. a shift from when something is considered a bargain to when it becomes a rip-off. But between these two points are more stages such as, too cheap, cheap, average, expensive and too expensive.

The same applies to our charts. The charts show us how the buyers and sellers behaved at a certain time in the past. This is translated through price action and does not mean that because there were lots of buyers at a certain base or level that that pattern will repeat. It just means there is high probability of a reaction in the buyers’ favor.

Our study here at RTM is not about picking tops and bottoms, it is about following along the path of the ITs once the signs are there, staying flexible to change and acting accordingly.

Now back to area 5:)

In my opinion ITs look for levels rather visually! and arrange them so that when they are approached and hit, they bring about all the orderflow they need for their fills! (that is what i thin IF means with - All the duckies are aligned

)

In the mean time, they prepare the battlefield for all the duckies and put the pendings there.

Hope this gives a different view. AERO

author: PASniper
text:
Hi guys,

I think that a huge weapon of the ITs are the news, and here I want to share with you my point of view with an example from today, with the USA Non-Farm Employment Change & Unemployment Rate:

1. Retail Traders go short by one of the most important news of the market (the result show a strong Dollar), meanwhile the IT and RTM traders (If you are doing the things right) are waiting the market to get to a huge demand area.

2. When it gets to the demand area the IT use the pending orders in the zone, the short positions and SL of all the traders that were trading the news to get to the TP (supply area) with a huge momentum (CPLQ).

This is the reason that I don’t like to trade the news, because the result of the news is not the reason and direction of the move, like many people say here: news only accelerate the things. I only use the news to stay out of the market and enter after the result.

I didn’t take the trade, but I think it was a beautiful one.

What do you think? This is just the point of view, from someone that is studying all the material here.
